projectBackground.name: Fintra Platform Migration
projectBackground.context: The first cloud invoice exceeded forecast, one storage bucket is public and the app runs in a single zone.

manager.name: Ciaran Doyle
manager.note: Cloud makes mistakes cheap to make and expensive to keep. Find them, price them and fix them in order of risk.

assignment.title: Cut cost, raise availability, close the gaps
assignment.brief: Calculate costs and downtime allowances, identify security misconfigurations and recommend an architecture.

documents.name: Instance Inventory
documents.note: 10 instances at $0.20 per hour, 730 hours per month; 6 are steady-state.

documents.name: Security Findings
documents.note: Public storage bucket, shared root credentials, no multi-factor authentication.

tasks.title: Reserved Pricing
tasks.prompt: 10 instances cost $0.20/hour for 730 hours. Six steady-state instances get a 40% reserved discount. What is the new monthly cost (USD)?
tasks.workingNote: Each instance: 0.20 x 730 = 146. Four on-demand = 584. Six reserved = 6 x 146 x 0.6 = 525.6. Total = 1,109.6.
tasks.reasoning: Commit discounts apply only to predictable workloads.
tasks.tip: Reserve steady load; keep spiky load on-demand.
tasks.mistake: Reserving everything wastes money on idle capacity.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Allowed Downtime
tasks.prompt: A 99.9% availability target over a 30-day month (43,200 minutes) allows how many minutes of downtime?
tasks.reasoning: Availability targets translate directly into downtime budgets.
tasks.tip: Express targets as minutes so teams grasp them.
tasks.mistake: Treating 99.9% as 'basically never' hides a real budget.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: High Availability
tasks.prompt: The app runs in one availability zone. What improves availability most directly?
options: Deploy across multiple availability zones behind a load balancer
Move to a different colour theme
tasks.reasoning: Multi-zone removes a single point of failure.
tasks.mistake: A bigger single instance remains a single failure point.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Shared Responsibility
tasks.prompt: Who is responsible for configuring access to the customer's storage bucket?
tasks.reasoning: Providers secure the platform; customers secure their configuration and data.
tasks.tip: Know your side of the line.
tasks.mistake: Assuming the provider handles it causes public buckets.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Security Fixes
tasks.prompt: Select the fixes you would prioritise.
options: Replace shared root credentials with least-privilege roles
tasks.reasoning: Remove public exposure and strengthen identity first.
tasks.mistake: Cosmetic changes leave the real risk untouched.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Recommendation
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence recommendation to the client on cost, availability and security.
tasks.modelAnswer: I recommend reserving the six steady-state instances to cut the monthly bill from $1,460 to about $1,110, a 24% saving. The platform should run across two availability zones to meet the 43-minute monthly downtime budget. Immediately make the storage bucket private, enable multi-factor authentication and replace shared root credentials with least-privilege roles. These changes cost little and remove the largest risks.
tasks.reasoning: A good recommendation quantifies the saving, ties to the target and orders security actions.
tasks.mistake: Advice without numbers is hard to approve.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Public Bucket
caseStudy.background: A company left a storage bucket public for months. Customer files were exposed and indexed by a search engine, triggering a regulatory notice.
caseStudy.budget: Regulatory fine and breach notification costs
caseStudy.solution: Cumulus added continuous configuration scanning and blocked public buckets by policy.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Automate guardrails; don't rely on memory.

quiz.q: The case study exposure was caused by:
options: A public bucket and no scanning
